question:
Context:

  • Using Google Cloud Composer to schedule and orchestrate some tasks.
  • There are around 20 active DAGs currently. It will grow over time (around 40-50).
  • Each DAG has 4 tasks. They are scheduled to run every hour.
  • Each task is a dbt run command. Every task selects specific set of models.
  • Each task typically take around 1-5 mins depending on the selected models. They are not very resource intensive. Total DAG run shouldnt take more than 10-15 mins.

My problem is that the workers not scaling even though there are 100s of tasks queued in celery.

As you can see below, tasks keep getting queued but the worker is not increasing.

This is my resource configuration:

And this is my only Airflow configuration that I have overriden:

What am I doing wrong here? Why is the active worker 0 even though minimum is 1? I know I dont need more resource per worker to execute the task because the tasks used to get executed before.

I have seen this answer already. It suggested to reduce the worker_concurrency (which is already small in my case) and increase the max_active_tasks_per_dag (this setting is useless because tasks need to run sequentially in my DAGs)

According to the documentation, it uses Scale Factor Target metric to scale the workers. I've checked the metric, and it keeps on increasing but the workers dont scale. It stays at 0 for some reason!
title: How to Resolve Workers Not Scaling with 100s of Queued Tasks in Google Cloud Composer?
answer:
Had this exact same issue over the weekend and bumped into this post while researching.

In my case this was a sign that worker did not have enough memory to handle the work that was scheduled. In order to get autoscaling to kick in your worker needs to have enough memory to handle work that is assigned to it, but autoscaling kicks in when you are scheduling more things than one worker can handle.

In your case with 2GB memory it is not enough and it fails. And your CPU is also too big.

Depending on your composer version there is some math how many tasks can fit in one worker by default. For your configuration it is for sure more than 10.

You keeping it low at 2 tasks with worker_concurrency tells worker to pick up only 2 tasks which is not enough for autoscaling to kick in.

My recommendation is:

  1. Use default value for worker_concurrency (In Airflow 2.6.3 and later versions, a minimum value out of 32, 12 * worker_CPU, and 6 * worker_memory)

  2. Monitor the environment fter your executions and then tweak the following settings one at a time

    1. core.parallelism
    2. celery.worker_concurrency
    3. core.max_active_tasks_per_dag
